title: Process is stuck and even SIGKILL won't kill it

turns.user_message: I tried to kill a stuck rsync process but `kill -9 <pid>` doesn't make it go away. `ps` shows the process is still there. The whole machine feels normal, this one process is just frozen. What's happening?
turns.se_response_summary: SIGKILL ignored = process in D state (uninterruptible sleep). Kernel can't deliver any signal until syscall returns. Two common holders: (1) Disk I/O hanging — NFS server gone, dying drive, multipath stuck. (2) FS op blocked. Diagnose with /proc/<pid>/stack (kernel call stack), /proc/<pid>/wchan (kernel function blocking), dmesg, mount. Map of wchan → cause: nfs_wait_on_request=NFS server; io_schedule=block I/O; cifs_demultiplex=SMB; fuse_get_req=FUSE userspace daemon hung.
hints: Why doesn't SIGKILL work on a D-state process?
What two files in /proc/<pid>/ tell you what subsystem is blocking?

turns.user_message: ps shows STAT=D wchan=nfs_wait_on_request. /proc/<pid>/stack shows nfs_wait_on_request → nfs_lock_and_join_requests → nfs_updatepage → vfs_write → ksys_write. dmesg shows 'nfs: server backup-nfs.acme.io not responding, still trying'.
turns.se_response_summary: Confirmed NFS hang on backup-nfs.acme.io. Two paths: (A) Fix the server (preferred) — once it accepts requests, kernel NFS retry succeeds, rsync continues. No client action needed. (B) Force client to give up if server permanently gone: sudo umount -fl /mnt/nfs/backup. -f=force (drop in-flight), -l=lazy (detach now). Kernel returns EIO to pending RPC, rsync syscall exits, queued SIGKILL fires. For prevention: fstab options soft,timeo=30,retrans=3 instead of default hard.
hints: What two flags to umount break the wait without waiting for the server?
What fstab option family prevents future hangs from being uninterruptible?

turns.user_message: umount -fl worked, process gone. Server's still down — turns out the NFS box's disk array failed. While we wait for ops to fix it, what could prevent this from happening again on a flaky network?
turns.se_response_summary: Three layers: (1) Mount options: read-mostly use soft+timeo+retrans; read-write keep hard but add intr+timeo. Prefer NFS v4.x. (2) systemd auto-recovery: define mount unit with TimeoutSec, plus a watchdog timer with OnUnitActiveSec=5min that resets-failed and restarts the mount. (3) Workload pattern: don't rsync directly to NFS; stage to local then ship via separate retry-able process. Keeps primary workload immune to NFS hiccups.
hints: What's the right mount-option set for read-mostly vs read-write workloads?
How do you architect around a flaky NFS dependency, not just tune around it?

turns.user_message: If wchan had shown `io_schedule` instead of an NFS function — different diagnosis?
turns.se_response_summary: io_schedule = block-device wait, not network FS. Different order: (1) dmesg | grep -E 'i/o error|sense key|aborted|smart' for hardware errors. (2) iostat -xz to find which device has high svctm/await. (3) ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd to match files to devices. (4) smartctl -a /dev/sdX for drive health (reallocated/pending sectors). (5) cat /proc/mdstat for RAID rebuild. (6) multipath -ll for failed paths. Fix depends: dying drive=replace, multipath=bounce path, RAID=wait or repair.
hints: What does io_schedule mean — network or block device?
What hardware-level signals tell you it's a dying drive?
